paras: Trachylepis nancycoutuae, also known commonly as Nancy Coutu's mabuya and Nancy Coutu's skink, is a species of lizard in the subfamily Lygosominae of the family Scincidae. The species is endemic to Madagascar.
The specific name, nancycoutuae, is in honor of American Peace Corps volunteer Nancy Coutu (1967–1996), who was murdered in Madagascar by cattle thieves.
The preferred natural habitats of Trachylepis nancycoutuae are rocky areas and shrubland, at altitudes of 700–750 m (2,300–2,460 ft).
The mode of reproduction of Trachylepis nancycoutuae is unknown.
